newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Thursday in line with soft Japanese prices and bouts of selling by local commodity houses, dealers said.

"Prices kept going down because of Japan and the fact that we ran into some selling by some of the commodity houses here," a local rubber trader said. "It's still a very hesistant market. China should be coming in because these prices are attractive, but credit is tight there and they have not been seen in the market," another trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark March contract slid 1.5 yen to end at 134.5 yen.
Kobe's March contract slipped 0.4 yen to settle at 134.3.
Another trader said: "Trading has been slow today and it may weaken further as we approach the weekend."
There was no reaction to the news that the Singapore Commodity Exchange was mulling changes in its TSR20 contract.

At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 124.75-125.25 U.S. cents a kg from 125.25 cents. November RSS1 was seen at 174.50-176.50 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.25) a kg from yesterday's settlement of 176.50 cents. November TSR20 was seen at 171.50-173.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.23) a kg against the previous 173.50 cents.
